question: Which Dravidian language was accorded the classical language status in 2004 by the Union Government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil** was accorded the **classical language status in 2004** by the Union Government of India.
 
• The status of a classical language is given to languages that have a rich heritage and independent nature.
 
• Tamil is one of the oldest languages in the world, with a recorded history spanning over 2000 years.
 
• This recognition highlights the cultural and historical significance of the Tamil language.
 
• Tamil literature, with its ancient texts and poetry, is a testament to the language's classical status.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kannada** and **Telugu** were later accorded the **classical language status in 2008**.
 
• **Malayalam** received the **classical language status in 2013**.
 
• The criteria for declaring a language as classical include its antiquity, a body of ancient literature or texts, and its original literary tradition.
 
• The classical language status is a recognition of the language's historical and cultural significance.
